study.question: Does the supplied-order advantage survive replacing lexical canonical ordering with two fixed, complete-event content-hash canonical orders at unchanged learned capacity, input information and training recipe?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: the original joint model/ordinal bridges obtain click AUC0.6685268680116033, while global lexical canonical_forward obtains0.6659442302433756 and canonical_reverse0.6660154869397665. However, lexical sorting changes which events share each of the ten compression blocks and imposes encoded-ID adjacency; these are alternative explanations for a loss attributed to order. Within-canonical0.6677110387593714 and blocks-canonical0.6660661992566252 localize sensitivity without isolating useful temporal information. Replacing coarse moments with local duplicates gives supplied0.6658825132684709 versus canonical0.6659956925288563, so whole-block sensitivity can disappear when information is removed. Single-moment and scrambled branches also lose AUC. Latest summary rotation with inherited initialization obtains0.6681452585892139; transporting consumers obtains0.6684626464055777 versus ordinal bridge0.6685268680116033; coefficient transport obtains0.6684701793164196. Thus much of the rotation loss is compatible with initialization/optimization, and residual differences remain unexplained. These are one frozen training seed, not independent repetitions. Provisional mechanism: if supplied order contributes useful association between content and event ranks beyond canonical grouping choices, it should outperform both content-only hash canonicalizations as well as lexical canonicalization. If a hash treatment recovers supplied performance or beats it at acceptable measured cost, the stronger claim that the observed loss requires useful supplied order is falsified for these replacements. No novelty or mechanism-confirmation claim is made.

nearest_work.difference: Direct architectural parent: retain its entire learned network and compression; add only a common complete-event reindexing operation before embeddings, target-match moments and all history compression. Parent source hash is checked against the workspace contract.

Closest local information-boundary control, full receipt/config read. Replace monotonically encoded-ID lexical priority by nonlinear bounded content-hash priority with exact complete-tuple fallback. No new learned capacity. Lexical cell bridges this existing result, while unchanged original remains utility/cost reference.

Archived original primary text read, lines56-105 describe target-conditioned local activation and weighted pooling. Inherit that operator through the existing action-aware adaptation; do not claim exact DIN reproduction or import original reported performance. This study changes layout before the inherited compressed scorer, not its attention mechanism.

Pinned benchmark forward lines175-204 flatten history then tokenize with context. Current study retains the pooled joint network and its existing ten blocks; no flattened-history tokenizer or UniMixing layer is adopted. Original-method equivalence and priority are not established.

Pinned benchmark forward lines113-152 pool history then tokenize fields/task readouts. Current study retains the existing local-activation network, towers and product correction; no HiFormer token interaction or external effectiveness claim.

study.proposed_difference: Before embedding, stable exact lexicographic sorting of complete valid event tuples supplies collision fallback for two fixed hash keys. Sequential modulo2147483647 mixing with seeds104729 and130363 uses int64 bounded arithmetic and no RNG, labels or original positions. Canonicalization fills the same valid destinations; every event field and each task mask uses the same source gather, preserving target and invalid positions. Four variants select hash_a/hash_b/lexical/supplied after executing the same three sorts. Hash canonicalization is invariant to arbitrary joint permutations of valid event tuples at fixed validity pattern, not invariant to changing the set of events, masks or history length. The two hash choices test replacement-layout dependence and are not independent scientific replications. No reparameterization, parameter transport, new optimizer, loss change or external model is introduced.
predictions: If useful supplied order is robust to these content-layout alternatives, supplied_workmatched should reproduce0.6685268680116033 within host numerical tolerance and exceed both hash variants and lexical_workmatched on validation click AUC; the unchanged incumbent stays the utility reference.

If lexical encoded-ID grouping accounts for a material part of the canonical gap, at least one hash treatment should improve on lexical at identical learned capacity. Recovery to supplied performance is evidence against necessity of supplied order in this tested architecture, not a claim that all histories are order-free.

Every canonical cell must return the same reindexed complete tuple tensors under arbitrary joint valid-event permutations, including full-tuple ties and forced hash collisions. Supplied bridge must retain parent semantics and all cells should measure32192421 parameters.

Hash/sort/gather work may increase inference cost versus the unchanged incumbent; no speed or efficiency benefit is predicted without measured throughput, latency and training cost. HashA/B sensitivity itself is evidence that replacement geometry remains consequential.
falsifiers: HashA or hashB matching or improving supplied click AUC at acceptable measured cost falsifies useful supplied-order necessity for that replacement; a single small difference needs repetition before a stable claim.

Both hash treatments below supplied, with correct boundary/parity checks, support only supplied-order utility relative to these tested replacements; they do not prove a temporal mechanism or refute every order-invariant model.

Layout invariance, per-task eligibility conservation, target/padding preservation, integer overflow, no-mutation, native backward or supplied parity failure invalidates interpretation and requires a charged correction before conclusions.

Material disagreement between lexical_workmatched and the historical lexical bridge makes cross-round AUC attribution unresolved until source/numerical differences are audited; do not silently treat the old result as matched.
alternative_explanations: Replacing event grouping changes nonlinear compression and training Dice normalization support; a supplied advantage could reflect more favorable grouping rather than semantic chronology.

Hash mixing is deterministic and not a proven uniform random assignment; encoded IDs and eligibility distributions can induce collisions or correlated priorities. Exact tuple fallback is invariant but may affect grouping.

Masks, history length and publisher offline-prefix construction remain predictive benchmark assumptions. No timestamps or real event-time intervals are available, and offline delayed actions need not be causally mature online.

Frozen one-pass optimization, initialization, BF16 reduction and coordinate-sensitive Adam can change outcomes despite equal representational capacity; transport results motivate caution rather than proving this explanation.

Two hash nuisance choices are not seed replications; repeated prior bridge equality at the same seed is reproducibility, not uncertainty quantification. Adaptive validation use and user exposure dependence constrain inference.

The joint model improves click AUC over DIN but worsens each auxiliary AUC (DIN0.84907/0.86490/0.87018 versus parent0.80498/0.81507/0.83050 approximately). Click selection does not establish all-task superiority.
